full_judgment: 11. On the other hand, the learned Counsel Mr Probir Neegi, appearing on behalf of the defendant-respondent-opposite party submits that the concurrent finding of facts cannot be disturbed unless it is manifestly perverse. The trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court is absolutely justified in dismissing the suit of the plaintiff because the plaintiff miserably failed to prove his possession over the suit land and, as such, the Courts below found that the suit is not maintainable and the suit is barred by limitation and it is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The Courts below rightly found that the plaintiff was not in possession of the suit land and in a suit for declaration the plaintiff cannot .seek any relief as such, the plaintiff ought to have filed a title suit with a prayer for recovery of khas possession. The learned Counsel further submits that the SA and RS Khatian was prepared long before but the plain- tiff did not take any steps for correction of the record if at all it would be wrongly prepared as such the suit of the plaintiff is barred by limitation. The learned Courts below rightly found that the suit was barred by limitation. The defendant examined as many as 5 (five) witnesses in this case to prove the right, title and possession of the suit land and all the DWs proved the case of the defendant with regard to the possession of the suit land. The learned Connsel next submits that both the Courts below concurrently found that the plaintiff Md Shafiuddin Ahmed and his brother Hashmat Ali purchased the suit land along with other land from Rajbari Bank on 15-1-1944 by way of registered deed and on the same day they sold the said property to one Mozaharuddin by a registered deed. Thereafter Mozaharuddin gave patta to the plaintiff by a registered deed dated 29-1-1944 and plaintiff also gave a registered kabuliat to Mozaharuddin on 29-1-1944. The learned Counsel submits that it appears to be an unusual transaction which creates a doubt and suspicion with regard to the genuineness of the document and for this reason the lower appellate Court as well as the trial Court disbelieved the documents. The finding of the Courts below are absolutely right and justified and it should not be disturbed in revision under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his contention the learned Counsel cited the case of Hazari Bala Sana and another vs Niron alias Niranjan Mondal and others reported in 1997 BLD (AD) 295 wherein it has been held that "It is a settled principle that the finding of facts, whether concurrent or not, arrived at by the Power appellate Court, which is the final Court of fact, is binding on the High Court Division, as a revisional to out except in certain well defined exceptional circumstances, such as non-consideration or misreading of the material evidence affecting the merit of the case. Finally, the learned Counsel submits that if the plaintiff would be in possession of the suit land certainly the RS and SA Khatian would be prepared in the name of the plaintiff and; as such, both the Courts below rightly observed that the plaintiff miserably failed to prove his right; title and possession over the suit land. Therefore the judgment passed by the Courts below do not call for any interference by this Court.
